L1_hard.summary: EMA trend participation with flow confirmation, volatility-regime caps, and multi-tier exposure rules.
L1_hard.query: Define volatility regime caps using current-bar indicators: if df['std_20'] >= 0.06 OR df['wvma_20'] >= 0.70 then the maximum allowed target position size is 0.50, else the maximum allowed target position size is 1.00. Next apply hard overrides that force a flat position: set target size to 0 if df['close'] < df['ema_90'] OR df['roc_5'] > 1.04 OR df['vstd_20'] > 2.00 OR df['ema_10'] < df['ema_30']. If not forced flat, apply an overbought de-risk rule: if df['rsi_14'] > 72 OR df['qtlu_40'] > 0.05 then cap the target position size at 0.25. Otherwise compute the base signal-strength size: set base size to 1.00 when df['ema_10'] > df['ema_30'] AND df['ema_30'] > df['ema_90'] AND df['imxd_30'] > 0.30 AND df['mfi_14'] > 50 AND df['vma_20'] < 0.95. Set base size to 0.50 when df['ema_10'] > df['ema_30'] AND df['imxd_30'] > 0.10 AND df['mfi_14'] > 45 AND df['min_10'] > 0.985. Set base size to 0.25 when df['ema_10'] > df['ema_30'] AND df['min_10'] > 0.990 AND df['rsi_14'] < 45; otherwise base size is 0. Final target position size on the bar is the base size clipped to the regime maximum, unless an override/cap above applies.

L1_hard.summary: Trend-filtered pullback entries with strict volatility and overbought risk overrides.
L1_hard.query: Start with risk overrides: set target position size to 0 if df['close'] < df['sma_100'] OR df['atr_14'] > 0.06*df['close'] OR df['std_20'] > 0.05 OR df['rsi_14'] > 72 OR df['klen'] > 0.08. If not risk-blocked, require a primary trend gate: df['close'] > df['sma_100'] AND df['sma_20'] > df['sma_50'] AND df['beta_60'] < 0.000. Within that gate, set size to 0.25 when df['rsi_14'] < 50 AND df['stoch_k_14'] < 45 AND df['ma_10'] < 1.01. Increase to 0.50 when the 0.25 conditions hold AND df['mfi_14'] < 45 AND df['imin_20'] < 0.25. Increase to 1.00 only when the 0.50 conditions hold AND df['ema_10'] > df['ema_20'] AND df['atr_14'] < 0.04*df['close']; otherwise keep the highest satisfied tier. Add a conservative exit/flat trigger even if trend-gated: size must be 0 whenever df['roc_5'] < 0.97 OR df['ma_5'] > 1.02.

L1_hard.summary: Fast momentum breakout participation scaled by strength and throttled by shock-risk caps.
L1_hard.query: Buy pressure is defined as df['rank_20'] > 0.75 AND df['cntp_5'] > 0.60 AND df['cci_20'] > 120, but apply priority risk rules first. If df['roc_3'] < 0.985 OR df['close'] < df['ema_20'] OR df['sumd_10'] < -0.20, set target size to 0 regardless of any other signals. If not flat, cap exposure to 0.25 when df['atr_14'] > 0.08*df['close'] OR df['klen'] > 0.10 OR df['wvma_20'] > 2.0 (shock/instability override). Otherwise, set size to 0.50 when df['rank_20'] > 0.75 AND df['cntp_5'] > 0.60 AND df['cci_20'] > 120 AND df['vsumd_10'] > 0.40. Escalate to 1.00 only if the 0.50 conditions hold AND df['rsv_14'] > 0.80 AND df['rsi_7'] > 55 AND df['cord_20'] > 0.20. Add a momentum fade exit: if df['stoch_k_14'] < df['stoch_d_14'] AND df['rsi_7'] < 45, force size to 0.

L1_hard.summary: Regime-aware sizing using volatility bands, volume-price coupling, and overheat de-risking.
L1_hard.query: Classify the current bar by volatility: treat as high-vol if df['std_20'] > 0.04, otherwise low-vol, and use this regime only to scale exposure (no state). Hard risk-off has top priority: set target size to 0 if df['std_20'] > 0.07 OR df['wvma_20'] > 2.2 OR df['beta_20'] > 0.0015 OR df['ma_10'] > 1.02. If not risk-off, define a base participation gate requiring df['beta_60'] < 0.000 AND df['cord_20'] > 0.15 AND df['mfi_14'] > 45 AND df['rsi_14'] > 45. In low-vol, set size to 0.60 when the base gate holds AND df['imxd_20'] > 0.20 AND df['sumd_20'] > 0.20; raise to 1.00 when additionally df['ema_20'] > df['ema_50'] AND df['rank_20'] > 0.65. In high-vol (df['std_20'] > 0.04), set size to 0.30 when the base gate holds AND df['imxd_20'] > 0.30 AND df['atr_14'] < 0.07*df['close'], and do not exceed 0.60 even if other entry conditions are strong. Finally, apply an overheat priority de-risk: if df['rank_20'] > 0.90 AND df['rsi_14'] > 72, cap size at 0.25 even if higher tiers are satisfied.

L1_hard.summary: Trend-filtered oversold reversals with candle confirmation and strict volatility-based risk overrides.
L1_hard.query: Start with hard risk overrides: set target position size to 0 if df['std_20'] > 0.05 OR df['atr_14'] > 0.05*df['close'] OR (df['klen'] > 0.09 AND df['kmid'] < 0) OR df['close'] < (df['sma_50'] - 2.0*df['atr_14']). Next, apply profit-taking/avoidance overrides (also force 0): df['rsi_14'] > 65 OR df['rank_20'] > 0.85 OR df['ma_20'] < 0.97. Only if none of the overrides trigger, allow buying and size by signal strength under the long-term trend filter df['close'] > df['sma_200'] AND df['sma_50'] > df['sma_200']. Set size to 1.0 if df['rank_20'] < 0.20 AND df['rsi_14'] < 30 AND df['mfi_14'] < 25 AND df['klow2'] > 0.55. Otherwise set size to 0.5 if df['rank_20'] < 0.30 AND df['rsi_14'] < 40 AND df['mfi_14'] < 35 AND df['klow2'] > 0.45; otherwise set size to 0.25 if df['rank_20'] < 0.35 AND df['rsi_14'] < 45 AND df['cntd_5'] < -0.20 AND df['klow2'] > 0.40; else size 0.

L1_hard.summary: Momentum burst entries scaled by ROC and volume-price coupling, with overheat throttles and reversal exits.
L1_hard.query: On every bar, enforce highest-priority crash controls: target position size is 0 if (df['klen'] > 0.12 AND df['kmid2'] < -0.40) OR df['rsi_14'] > 88 OR df['atr_14'] > 0.08*df['close']. Next, apply reversal exits that also force 0 regardless of any entry signal: df['stoch_k_14'] < df['stoch_d_14'] OR df['roc_2'] > 1.01 OR df['rank_50'] < 0.55. If not flat by the above, apply an overheat throttle that caps exposure at 0.4 when df['ma_5'] < 0.97 AND df['rsi_14'] > 75 (this throttle has priority over the sizing tiers below). Otherwise, size aggressively by momentum strength: set size to 1.0 if df['roc_5'] < 0.96 AND df['ma_10'] < 0.985 AND df['stoch_k_14'] > 85 AND (df['stoch_k_14'] > df['stoch_d_14']) AND df['cord_10'] > 0.35 AND df['imax_20'] < 0.15 AND df['vsumd_10'] > 0.30. If that is not satisfied, set size to 0.7 if df['roc_5'] < 0.98 AND df['stoch_k_14'] > 75 AND df['cord_10'] > 0.20 AND df['imax_20'] < 0.25; else set size to 0.4 if df['roc_3'] < 0.99 AND df['stoch_k_14'] > 65 AND df['vsumd_5'] > 0.20; else 0.

L1_hard.summary: Pullback-in-uptrend entries with volatility-capped exposure and layered risk and profit-taking overrides.
L1_hard.query: Define strict priority rules first: set target position size to 0 if df['atr_14'] > 0.07*df['close'] OR df['std_20'] > 0.07 OR df['klen'] > 0.10 OR df['kmid'] < -0.04 OR df['close'] < (df['sma_120'] - 2.5*df['atr_14']). If not forced flat, take profits/avoid overextension by setting size to 0 when df['rsv_14'] > 0.85 OR df['rsi_7'] > 72 OR df['qtlu_20'] > 0.04. If still eligible to buy, compute a volatility cap from df['std_20']: cap = 1.0 when df['std_20'] < 0.03; cap = 0.6 when 0.03 <= df['std_20'] <= 0.05; cap = 0.3 when 0.05 < df['std_20'] <= 0.07. Next compute a base signal size using only current-bar conditions under a trend filter df['close'] > df['sma_120'] AND df['sma_30'] > df['sma_120']: base = 1.0 if df['rsv_14'] < 0.30 AND df['rsi_7'] < 45 AND df['corr_20'] > 0.15 AND df['vsumd_10'] > 0.00; else base = 0.6 if df['rsv_14'] < 0.40 AND df['rsi_7'] < 50 AND df['corr_20'] > 0.05; else base = 0.3 if df['rsv_14'] < 0.45 AND df['cntd_10'] < -0.10; else base = 0. Finally, set target position size to the smaller of (base, cap) on that bar.

L1_hard.summary: Uptrend-only dip entries with strict volatility and candle-shock overrides and tiered sizing.
L1_hard.query: Start with risk overrides: set target position size to 0.0 if df['std_20'] > 0.06 OR df['klen'] > 0.07 OR df['vstd_20'] > 1.8. If risk overrides are not triggered, require an uptrend filter df['close'] > df['sma_200'] AND df['sma_50'] > df['sma_200']; if this filter fails, set position size to 0.0. Under the uptrend filter, size entries by dip severity: set size to 0.25 if df['rsv_14'] < 0.35 AND df['mfi_14'] < 45; increase to 0.50 if df['rsv_14'] < 0.25 AND df['mfi_14'] < 35 AND df['cntd_5'] < -0.20. Only allow full size 1.00 when df['rsv_14'] < 0.20 AND df['mfi_14'] < 30 AND df['min_20'] > 0.985 AND df['klow2'] > 0.55. Apply a priority de-risking rule that forces size back to 0.0 if df['rsi_14'] > 72 OR df['rsv_14'] > 0.80 OR df['close'] < df['sma_50'] - 1.5*df['atr_14'], even if the entry tiers above are satisfied.

L1_hard.summary: Near-high momentum breakout sizing using rank, max-ratio, volume-flow coupling, and heat caps.
L1_hard.query: Enter on momentum continuation and scale exposure with strength, but first set target size to 0.0 if df['std_10'] > 0.10 OR df['wvma_20'] > 2.5 (these risk conditions override everything). If risk is acceptable, set size to 1.00 when df['rank_20'] > 0.85 AND df['max_20'] < 1.015 AND df['roc_3'] < 0.985 AND df['vsumd_10'] > 0.25 AND df['cord_20'] > 0.10. Set size to 0.50 when df['rank_20'] > 0.75 AND df['max_20'] < 1.03 AND df['roc_5'] < 0.97 AND df['vsumd_10'] > 0.10, and set size to 0.25 when df['rank_20'] > 0.65 AND df['roc_3'] < 0.995. Apply an overheat priority cap: if df['rsi_6'] > 88 OR df['rsv_9'] > 0.90, then the position size must not exceed 0.25 even if stronger entry criteria are met. Exit to 0.0 whenever df['rank_20'] < 0.35 OR df['roc_3'] > 1.02 OR df['sumd_5'] < -0.40.

L1_hard.summary: Volatility-regime sizing that switches between low-vol mean reversion and higher-vol trend follow-through.
L1_hard.query: Use strict priority rules: immediately set target position size to 0.0 if df['klen'] > 0.08 OR df['std_20'] > 0.09 OR df['corr_30'] < -0.30. If not forced to zero, apply a heat throttle where df['rsi_6'] > 85 AND df['rsv_14'] > 0.85 caps the maximum position size at 0.25 regardless of other signals. In a low-volatility regime (df['std_20'] <= 0.035), take mean-reversion entries sized by extremity: set size to 0.50 if df['min_20'] > 0.985 AND df['rsi_14'] < 38 AND df['mfi_14'] < 45 AND df['vma_20'] < 1.10, and increase to 0.75 if df['min_20'] > 0.990 AND df['rsi_14'] < 32 AND df['klow2'] > 0.60 AND df['mfi_14'] < 40. In a higher-volatility regime (0.035 < df['std_20'] <= 0.09), follow the trend but keep sizing moderate: set size to 0.25 if df['sma_20'] > df['sma_60'] AND df['imxd_20'] > 0.30 AND df['sumd_10'] > 0.15, and increase to 0.50 if those conditions hold AND df['rsv_14'] > 0.55 AND df['vsumd_10'] > 0.20. Exit to 0.0 if df['sma_20'] < df['sma_60'] OR df['rsi_14'] > 68 OR df['mfi_14'] > 80.

L1_hard.summary: Defensive dip-buying in a structural uptrend with wick confirmation and strict risk overrides.
L1_hard.query: Start by applying risk priority rules: set target position size to 0 if df['std_20'] > 0.045 OR df['klen'] > 0.075 OR df['rsi_14'] > 82. Otherwise, require a long-term uptrend filter df['ma_200'] < 1.02 AND a medium-term confirmation df['sma_50'] > df['sma_200']; if either fails, target size is 0. If the trend filter passes and a capitulation-style dip occurs (df['bb_lower_20'] > df['close'] AND df['mfi_14'] < 22 AND df['klow2'] > 0.55), target size is 1.0; if it is a milder dip (df['bb_middle_20'] > df['close'] AND df['mfi_14'] < 30 AND df['rsi_14'] < 38), target size is 0.5; otherwise target size is 0.25 only when df['rsi_14'] < 42 AND df['mfi_14'] < 45. Add a profit-protection priority: if df['close'] > df['bb_upper_20'] AND df['rsi_14'] > 72, cap the target size at 0.25 even if entry signals are stronger. Finally, set target size to 0 whenever df['roc_5'] < 0.985 (fast deterioration filter) regardless of other non-risk entry conditions.

L1_hard.summary: High-frequency breakout continuation using band breaks, volume pressure, and momentum thrust scaling.
L1_hard.query: Buy pressure is defined first, but risk still overrides: if df['std_10'] > 0.085 OR df['rsi_7'] > 90, set target position size to 0 immediately. If risk is acceptable and df['close'] > df['bb_upper_20'] AND df['vma_20'] < 0.80 AND df['cci_20'] > 180 AND df['cord_10'] > 0.25, target size is 1.0 (maximum thrust condition). If the breakout is present but weaker (df['close'] > df['bb_upper_20'] AND df['vma_20'] < 0.90 AND df['cci_20'] > 120), target size is 0.6; if only early momentum shows (df['close'] > df['bb_middle_20'] AND df['cci_20'] > 80 AND df['stoch_k_14'] > 70), target size is 0.3. Enforce a conflict rule: if df['close'] < df['bb_middle_20'] OR df['cci_20'] < 0, target size becomes 0 even when other momentum conditions are true. Add a sharp mean-reversion fade safeguard: if df['kup2'] > 0.70 AND df['rsi_7'] > 85, cap target size at 0.3 rather than 1.0.

L1_hard.summary: Trend-aligned pullback entries with volatility-bucket sizing and flow confirmation for steadier compounding.
L1_hard.query: Determine the volatility bucket first using df['std_20']: if df['std_20'] >= 0.070 OR df['klen'] >= 0.090, target position size is 0 (hard risk cutoff). Otherwise, set a base maximum size of 1.0 when df['std_20'] < 0.030, 0.6 when 0.030 <= df['std_20'] < 0.050, and 0.3 when 0.050 <= df['std_20'] < 0.070. Only allow entries when the trend is positive across two windows (df['sma_30'] > df['sma_90'] AND df['sumd_20'] > 0.10 AND df['vsumd_20'] > 0.10); if not, target size is 0 regardless of the volatility bucket. Within that allowed regime, set target size to the base maximum when df['rsv_14'] < 0.25 AND df['stoch_k_14'] < 35 AND df['rsi_14'] < 45 (deep pullback), but cut it to half of the base maximum when df['rsv_14'] is between 0.25 and 0.40 (i.e., df['rsv_14'] >= 0.25 AND df['rsv_14'] < 0.40) with df['stoch_k_14'] < 45. Apply a priority exit/trim rule: if df['rsv_14'] > 0.78 OR df['stoch_k_14'] > 85 OR df['rsi_14'] > 74, set target size to 0. Finally, if df['cntd_10'] < -0.40 (recent return imbalance against you), cap target size at 0.3 even when deeper pullback conditions suggest a larger allocation.

L1_hard.summary: Low-volatility trend participation with strict risk overrides and stepped exposure increases.
L1_hard.query: Start each bar by applying hard risk overrides: set position size to 0 if df['close'] < df['sma_200'] OR df['std_20'] > 0.060 OR df['klen'] > 0.100. If the risk overrides are not triggered, apply a de-risk cap of 0.25 when df['atr_14'] > 0.040 * df['close'] OR df['rsi_14'] > 72. Otherwise, assign position size based on signal strength using nested conditions: set size to 1.00 only if (df['sma_50'] > df['sma_200']) AND (df['close'] > df['sma_50']) AND (df['macd'] > df['macd_signal']) AND (df['mfi_14'] > 55) AND (df['std_20'] < 0.035). Set size to 0.50 if (df['sma_50'] > df['sma_200']) AND (df['close'] > df['sma_50']) AND (df['macd'] > df['macd_signal']) AND (df['rsi_14'] >= 45) AND (df['rsi_14'] <= 65), but any df['vstd_20'] > 0.90 reduces that 0.50 to 0.25. Set size to 0.25 if (df['sma_50'] > df['sma_200']) AND (df['close'] > df['sma_200']) AND (df['rsi_14'] >= 40) AND (df['rsi_14'] <= 60), and set 0 otherwise. Exit logic is also evaluated per bar: if df['close'] < df['sma_50'] OR df['macd_hist'] < 0 OR df['mfi_14'] < 45, then position size must be 0 regardless of any entry sizing.

L1_hard.summary: Momentum ignition using CCI and MACD thrust with volume-change correlation and heat throttles.
L1_hard.query: Enter with a momentum-thrust template and size up with strength, but let risk signals override everything. First, force position size to 0 if df['atr_14'] > 0.070 * df['close'] OR df['klen'] > 0.120 OR df['beta_10'] < -0.006. If not risk-blocked, apply an overheat throttle: if df['rsi_7'] > 88 OR df['stoch_k_14'] > 92, cap position size at 0.25 even if all entry conditions are strong. Otherwise, set position size to 1.00 when (df['macd_hist'] > 0) AND (df['cci_20'] > 150) AND (df['cord_10'] > 0.25) AND (df['vsumd_10'] > 0.40) AND (df['close'] > df['ema_9']). Set position size to 0.50 when (df['macd_hist'] > 0) AND (df['cci_20'] > 100) AND (df['cord_10'] > 0.10) AND (df['close'] > df['ema_9']), but reduce that 0.50 to 0.25 if df['rsi_7'] < 55. If none of those sizing rules apply, set position size to 0. For exits on any bar, require position size to be 0 when df['macd_hist'] < 0 OR df['cci_20'] < 0 OR df['cord_10'] < -0.05, even if other factors are favorable.

L1_hard.summary: Trend-aligned dip accumulation with volatility-bucket sizing and clear priority-based exits.
L1_hard.query: The goal is to buy controlled pullbacks inside a confirmed uptrend, while scaling exposure down when volatility is elevated. Apply priority risk rules first: set position size to 0 if df['close'] < df['sma_100'] OR df['sma_20'] < df['sma_100'] OR df['mfi_14'] < 35. If the trend/risk gate passes, impose a volatility cap: if df['std_20'] >= 0.060 OR df['atr_14'] > 0.050 * df['close'], then position size cannot exceed 0.25 regardless of dip strength. Otherwise, size by dip severity using current-bar conditions: set size to 1.00 if (df['ma_10'] > 1.030) AND (df['rsi_14'] < 35) AND (df['rsv_14'] < 0.20) AND (df['close'] > df['sma_100']). Set size to 0.75 if (df['ma_10'] > 1.015) AND (df['rsi_14'] < 45) AND (df['rsv_14'] < 0.35) AND (df['std_20'] < 0.045), else set size to 0.25 if (df['ma_10'] > 1.005) AND (df['rsi_14'] <= 55) AND (df['rsv_14'] < 0.50). Profit-taking and exit are evaluated each bar and override sizing: if df['ma_10'] < 0.995 OR df['rsi_14'] > 65 OR df['rsv_14'] > 0.80, then position size must be 0.

L1_hard.summary: Low-volatility, volume-confirmed trend participation with strict risk-off priority overrides and tiered exposure.
L1_hard.query: Apply a hard risk-off rule first: set target position to 0 if df['std_20'] > 0.06 OR df['atr_14'] > 0.05*df['close'] OR df['klen'] > 0.10 OR df['rsi_14'] > 80. If none of those triggers, set target position to 1.0 when df['corr_60'] > 0.45 AND df['vsumd_20'] > 0.40 AND df['ma_200'] < 0.995 AND df['rsi_14'] >= 45 AND df['rsi_14'] <= 60. Otherwise set target position to 0.5 when df['corr_60'] > 0.25 AND df['vsumd_20'] > 0.20 AND df['ma_200'] < 1.000 AND df['vma_20'] < 0.95 AND df['rsi_14'] >= 40 AND df['rsi_14'] <= 65. Otherwise set target position to 0.25 when df['corr_60'] > 0.20 AND df['vma_20'] < 0.97 AND df['ma_200'] < 1.005, else set it to 0. Finally, regardless of the size chosen above, override to 0 if df['macd'] < df['macd_signal'] OR df['ma_50'] > 1.01 OR df['close'] > df['bb_upper_20'].

L1_hard.summary: Fast momentum thrust sizing using return/volume dominance, with overheat caps and rapid failure exits.
L1_hard.query: Set target position to 0 immediately if df['atr_14'] > 0.09*df['close'] OR df['klen'] > 0.14 OR df['roc_3'] > 1.02 OR df['close'] < df['ema_10'] (risk/impulse failure has priority over any entry). If risk-off is not triggered, assign 1.0 exposure when df['roc_5'] < 0.95 AND df['sumd_10'] > 0.75 AND df['vsumd_10'] > 0.50 AND df['rsv_14'] > 0.90 AND df['vma_5'] < 0.80. Otherwise assign 0.75 exposure when df['roc_5'] < 0.97 AND df['sumd_10'] > 0.60 AND df['rsv_14'] > 0.85 AND df['vsumd_10'] > 0.30; otherwise assign 0.40 exposure when df['roc_5'] < 0.98 AND df['sumd_10'] > 0.40 AND df['rsv_14'] > 0.75, else 0. Add an overheat throttle that overrides the above sizes: if df['qtlu_20'] > 0.10 OR df['rsi_7'] > 92, cap the target position at 0.25. For exits based on current-bar weakness, force target position to 0 whenever df['sumd_5'] < -0.20 OR df['vsumd_5'] < -0.20.

L1_hard.summary: Recent-low rebound entries gated by trend alignment and window-position metrics, with volatility-adjusted tiers.
L1_hard.query: Begin with priority risk filters: set target position to 0 if df['std_20'] > 0.07 OR df['imxd_20'] > 0.70 OR df['imxd_20'] < -0.70 OR df['mfi_14'] > 85. If those do not apply, use a rebound setup only when df['sma_50'] > df['sma_200'] AND df['imin_20'] < 0.15 AND df['rank_60'] < 0.35 AND df['stoch_k_14'] < 25 AND df['mfi_14'] < 35; then set target position to 1.0 if df['std_20'] < 0.035, else set it to 0.60 if df['std_20'] < 0.05, else set it to 0.30. If the strict rebound setup is not met, allow a weaker entry at 0.25 when df['sma_50'] > df['sma_200'] AND df['imin_20'] < 0.25 AND df['rank_60'] < 0.45 AND df['stoch_k_14'] < 35 AND df['rsi_14'] < 45 AND df['std_20'] < 0.05; otherwise set target position to 0. Independent of the above sizing, force target position to 0 when (df['close'] > df['bb_middle_20'] AND df['stoch_k_14'] > 70) OR df['close'] < df['bb_lower_20'].

L1_hard.summary: Quantile-based dip buying inside a long-term uptrend with strict risk-off overrides.
L1_hard.query: First apply hard risk overrides: set target position to 0 if df['close'] < df['sma_200'] OR df['std_20'] > 0.06 OR df['klen'] > 0.10 OR df['rsi_14'] > 75. If risk overrides are not triggered and df['close'] > df['sma_200'] AND df['sma_50'] > df['sma_200'], size the position by signal strength using df['qtld_80'], df['rsi_14'], df['mfi_14'], and df['klow2']. Set size to 1.00 when df['qtld_80'] < -0.06 AND df['rsi_14'] < 25 AND df['mfi_14'] < 20 AND df['klow2'] > 0.60. Else set size to 0.50 when df['qtld_80'] < -0.03 AND df['rsi_14'] < 35 AND df['mfi_14'] < 35 AND df['klow2'] > 0.45; else set size to 0.25 when df['qtld_80'] < -0.015 AND df['rsi_14'] < 45 AND df['mfi_14'] < 45; otherwise set size to 0. Profit-taking has priority after risk but before adding size: force size to 0 if df['qtlu_80'] > 0.03 OR df['ma_20'] < 0.985 OR (df['rsi_14'] > 62 AND df['mfi_14'] > 65).

L1_hard.summary: High-momentum thrust entries scaled by stochastic/CCI and volume spikes, with overheat throttles.
L1_hard.query: Buy aggressively when momentum and participation align: require df['kmid'] > 0.008 AND df['vma_20'] < 0.70 AND df['stoch_k_14'] > df['stoch_d_14'] AND df['cci_20'] > 120 to allow any nonzero position. Position sizing is tiered: set size to 1.00 if df['stoch_k_14'] > 92 AND df['cci_20'] > 220 AND df['vma_20'] < 0.55 AND df['kup2'] < 0.20; else set size to 0.66 if df['stoch_k_14'] > 85 AND df['cci_20'] > 170 AND df['vma_20'] < 0.65; else set size to 0.33 if df['stoch_k_14'] > 75 AND df['cci_20'] > 130; otherwise set size to 0. Set target to 0.6 when df['rsv_20'] > 0.88 AND df['rank_20'] > 0.85 AND df['cci_20'] > 100 AND df['cord_20'] > 0.20 AND df['vma_20'] < 0.90; otherwise set target to 0.3 when df['rsv_20'] > 0.85 AND df['cci_20'] > 80 AND df['vma_20'] < 1.00, else 0.0. Risk overrides supersede all entry sizing: force target to 0.0 if df['beta_5'] > 0.004 OR df['rsv_20'] < 0.55 OR df['cci_20'] < 0 OR df['vma_20'] > 1.25. Add a fast profit-lock rule: if df['qtlu_20'] > 0.030 AND df['rsi_7'] > 78, cap target at 0.5 even if the 1.0 tier is triggered.

L1_hard.summary: Volatility-aware swing participation with base sizing from risk metrics and pullback-sensitive boosts.
L1_hard.query: Treat risk as a gatekeeper: immediately set target position to 0.0 if df['atr_14'] > 0.070*df['close'] OR df['std_30'] > 0.060 OR df['corr_30'] < -0.25. If risk is acceptable, compute a base exposure from df['std_30']: base = 1.0 when df['std_30'] < 0.025, base = 0.6 when 0.025 <= df['std_30'] < 0.040, otherwise base = 0.3. Only activate base exposure when df['imxd_30'] > 0.25 AND df['rank_30'] > 0.25 AND df['rank_30'] < 0.80 AND df['cntd_10'] > 0.20 AND df['sumd_10'] > 0.15 AND df['kmid2'] > 0.10; if any of these fail, set target to 0.0. Apply a pullback boost for better reward-to-risk: if the activation block is true AND df['mfi_14'] < 40 AND df['rsv_14'] < 0.55 AND df['imin_20'] < 0.25, increase target by 0.2 but cap at 1.0. Profit-taking has priority over boosts: if df['qtlu_40'] > 0.025 AND df['rsv_14'] > 0.85, cap target at 0.3 regardless of the base/boost. A hard defensive exit overrides everything: set target to 0.0 if df['qtld_40'] < -0.020 OR df['cntd_5'] < -0.40.

L1_hard.summary: Defensive Bollinger mean-reversion with trend gate, strict risk overrides, and tiered exposure.
L1_hard.query: The objective is to buy controlled mean-reversion only when the long-term trend is supportive, with risk overrides taking absolute priority. First apply hard risk-off overrides: set target position to 0 if df['close'] < df['sma_200'] OR (df['atr_14'] / df['close']) > 0.05 OR df['std_20'] > 0.06 OR df['ksft2'] < -0.60. Next apply profit-taking clamps: set target position to 0 if df['close'] > df['bb_upper_20'] OR df['rsi_14'] > 65. Otherwise size by signal strength using nested conditions: set target position to 1.00 if (df['close'] < df['bb_lower_20']) AND (df['rsi_14'] < 25) AND (df['mfi_14'] < 20) AND (df['ma_50'] < 1.02); set to 0.50 if (df['close'] < df['bb_lower_20']) AND (df['rsi_14'] < 32) AND (df['mfi_14'] < 35) AND (df['ma_50'] < 1.03). If neither tier triggers but df['close'] < df['bb_middle_20'] AND df['rsi_14'] < 40 AND df['ma_50'] < 1.02, set target position to 0.25; else set it to 0.

L1_hard.summary: High-frequency near-high momentum participation with volume-price coupling and overheat throttles.
L1_hard.query: Buy aggressively when price is pressing recent highs with strong volume coupling, and downshift immediately on momentum failure. Apply priority risk throttles first: if df['rsi_14'] > 88 OR df['close'] < df['ema_50'], set target position to 0; else if df['rsi_14'] > 80 OR df['std_10'] > 0.09 OR (df['atr_14'] / df['close']) > 0.07, cap the target position at 0.30 regardless of other signals. Next, if df['macd_hist'] < 0 OR df['cord_10'] < 0, set target position to 0 (momentum/participation failure override). Otherwise use tiered sizing for breakout pressure: set target position to 1.00 if (df['max_20'] < 1.002) AND (df['imax_20'] < 0.10) AND (df['vma_20'] < 0.60) AND (df['cord_10'] > 0.40) AND (df['rank_20'] > 0.85); set to 0.60 if (df['max_20'] < 1.006) AND (df['vma_20'] < 0.75) AND (df['cord_10'] > 0.20) AND (df['rank_20'] > 0.75). If only (df['rank_20'] > 0.70) AND (df['cord_10'] > 0.10) AND (df['vma_20'] < 0.90) holds, set target position to 0.30; otherwise set it to 0.

L1_hard.summary: Volatility-bucket base exposure combined with quantile-based value timing and trend-confirmed participation.
L1_hard.query: Start by assigning a base exposure from current volatility, then modulate it using value, trend, and risk priorities. Define the base target position as 1.00 if df['std_20'] <= 0.03, 0.60 if 0.03 < df['std_20'] <= 0.06, 0.30 if 0.06 < df['std_20'] <= 0.09, and 0 if df['std_20'] > 0.09. Apply hard overrides before any entry: set target position to 0 if df['close'] < df['ema_60'] OR (df['atr_14'] / df['close']) > 0.06 OR df['klen'] > 0.08. Apply profit-taking next: set target position to 0 if df['qtlu_60'] > 0.05 OR df['rsi_14'] > 70. Otherwise, set the final target position as a fraction of the base using nested signal strength: use 1.00×base if (df['ema_20'] > df['ema_60']) AND (df['qtld_60'] < -0.04) AND (df['imxd_30'] > 0.20) AND (df['cntd_10'] > 0.20); use 0.50×base if (df['ema_20'] > df['ema_60']) AND (df['qtld_60'] < -0.02) AND (df['imxd_30'] > 0.10) AND (df['cntd_10'] > 0.10). If neither tier triggers but df['ema_20'] > df['ema_60'] AND df['qtld_60'] < -0.01, use 0.25×base; else set target position to 0.

L1_hard.summary: Low-volatility trend participation with strict risk overrides and tiered confirmation-based exposure sizing.
L1_hard.query: Begin each bar by applying a hard risk-off override: set target position size to 0 if df['close'] < df['sma_100'] OR df['macd_hist'] < 0 OR df['atr_14'] > 0.06*df['close'] OR df['rsi_14'] > 78. If none of those are true, set target position size to 1.0 only when df['std_20'] < 0.018 AND df['close'] > df['bb_upper_20'] AND df['macd'] > df['macd_signal'] AND df['vma_20'] < 0.85 AND df['mfi_14'] > 55. Otherwise, set target position size to 0.5 when df['std_20'] < 0.018 AND df['close'] > df['bb_middle_20'] AND df['macd'] > df['macd_signal'] AND df['vma_20'] < 0.85. If that is not met, set target position size to 0.25 when df['std_20'] < 0.020 AND df['close'] > df['bb_middle_20'] AND df['macd_hist'] > 0 AND df['mfi_14'] >= 45 AND df['mfi_14'] <= 55; otherwise set target position size to 0.

L1_hard.summary: Fast momentum thrust sizing using short EMAs and volume-pressure, with overheat and breakdown priority clamps.
L1_hard.query: Buy aggressively by setting target position size to 1.0 when df['ema_5'] > df['ema_13'] AND df['macd_hist'] > 0 AND df['rsv_9'] > 0.75 AND df['vsumd_10'] > 0.35 AND df['rsi_6'] > 62. If that full-strength condition is not met, set target position size to 0.7 when df['ema_5'] > df['ema_13'] AND df['rsv_9'] > 0.65 AND df['vsumd_10'] > 0.15 AND df['rsi_6'] > 55; else set it to 0.4 when df['macd_hist'] > 0 AND df['rank_20'] > 0.70 AND df['rsi_14'] > 55. Apply an overheat clamp with higher priority than the momentum sizing above: if df['rsi_3'] > 92 OR df['qtlu_20'] > 0.05, set target position size to 0.25 even if momentum conditions request more. Apply a final hard stop override with highest priority: if df['close'] < df['ema_34'] OR df['cci_20'] < -150 OR df['cntd_10'] < -0.60 OR df['atr_14'] > 0.09*df['close'], set target position size to 0 regardless of any other signals.

L1_hard.summary: Accumulation-trend alignment with correlation-based confirmation and volatility-sensitive sizing plus profit-protection clamps.
L1_hard.query: Prioritize safety first: set target position size to 0 if df['close'] < df['sma_200'] OR df['cord_10'] < -0.20 OR df['std_20'] > 0.070 OR df['klen'] > 0.12. Next, if df['qtlu_40'] > 0.08 OR df['rsi_14'] > 80, cap exposure by setting target position size to 0.25 even if other entry criteria are satisfied. Otherwise, when df['close'] > df['sma_50'] AND df['sma_50'] > df['sma_200'] AND df['cord_10'] > 0.20 AND df['corr_20'] > 0.15 AND df['vma_20'] < 0.90, set target position size based on volatility: 1.0 if df['std_20'] < 0.025, 0.6 if df['std_20'] >= 0.025 AND df['std_20'] < 0.045, else 0.35. If that strong alignment block is not met, set target position size to 0.3 when df['close'] > df['sma_200'] AND df['macd_hist'] > 0 AND df['cord_10'] > 0.10 AND df['corr_20'] > 0.05; otherwise set target position size to 0.

L1_hard.summary: Trend-filtered, accumulation-confirmed dip entries with strict risk overrides and tiered exposure caps.
L1_hard.query: Start with a hard risk override: set target exposure to 0 if df['close'] < df['sma_200'] OR df['std_20'] > 0.050 OR df['vstd_20'] > 1.00 OR df['obv'] < df['obv'].shift(10). If the risk override is not triggered, define a de-risk cap that limits exposure to at most 0.25 whenever df['close'] > df['bb_upper_20'] OR df['rsi_14'] > 70 OR df['kup2'] > 0.60. Otherwise, size the position by signal strength using the following tiers: set exposure to 1.00 if df['ema_20'] > df['ema_50'] AND df['mfi_14'] < 25 AND df['stoch_k_14'] < 20 AND df['corr_30'] > 0.10; set exposure to 0.50 if df['ema_20'] > df['ema_50'] AND df['mfi_14'] < 35 AND df['stoch_k_14'] < 30; set exposure to 0.25 if df['ema_50'] > df['sma_200'] AND df['mfi_14'] < 45. If none of the tier conditions are met, set exposure to 0.

L1_hard.summary: Fast momentum continuation using near-high positioning, volume surges, and candlestick impulse sizing.
L1_hard.query: Buy aggressively when price is pressing recent highs and volume spikes, using df['rank_20'], df['rsv_14'], df['imax_20'], and df['vma_20'] for explicit sizing tiers. Set target exposure to 1.00 if df['rank_20'] > 0.85 AND df['rsv_14'] > 0.80 AND df['imax_20'] <= 0.10 AND df['vma_20'] < 0.70 AND df['kmid2'] > 0.40; set exposure to 0.75 if df['rank_20'] > 0.85 AND df['rsv_14'] > 0.80 AND df['imax_20'] <= 0.10 AND df['vma_20'] < 0.90; set exposure to 0.50 if df['rank_20'] > 0.75 AND df['rsv_14'] > 0.70 AND df['imax_20'] <= 0.20. Apply a priority risk shutdown that forces exposure to 0 if (df['kmid2'] < -0.50 AND df['klen'] > 0.060) OR (df['stoch_k_14'] < df['stoch_d_14'] AND df['rank_20'] < 0.40) OR df['std_10'] > 0.070. If the risk shutdown is not active but the move looks overextended, cap exposure at 0.25 whenever df['rsi_6'] > 85 OR df['kup2'] > 0.70 OR df['max_10'] > 1.05; otherwise use the tiered exposure above, and set exposure to 0 when none of the entry tiers are satisfied.

L1_hard.summary: Dual-mode trend-and-pullback participation with volatility regime caps and layered profit-protection throttles.
L1_hard.query: Determine a volatility cap from the current bar: if df['std_20'] > 0.045 then maximum allowed exposure is 0.50, else maximum allowed exposure is 1.00. Impose top-priority defensive exits by setting exposure to 0 if df['close'] < df['sma_100'] OR (df['close'] < df['bb_lower_20'] AND df['kmid'] < -0.015) OR df['beta_20'] < -0.002. When not in a defensive exit state, compute a base exposure from two entry paths: set base exposure to 0.75 if df['ema_12'] > df['ema_48'] AND df['macd'] > df['macd_signal'] AND df['cord_20'] > 0.15; set base exposure to 1.00 if df['ema_12'] > df['ema_48'] AND df['min_20'] > 0.97 AND df['rsi_14'] >= 35 AND df['rsi_14'] <= 55. Add a profit-protection priority rule that caps exposure at 0.25 whenever df['max_20'] > 1.08 OR df['rsi_14'] > 75 OR df['close'] > df['bb_upper_20'], regardless of which entry path fired. Finally, set target exposure to the minimum of (base exposure, the volatility cap), and set exposure to 0 if neither entry path conditions are met.

L1_hard.summary: Trend-filtered oversold entries with strict risk overrides and tiered exposure reduction near highs.
L1_hard.query: Apply rules in strict priority order to set the target position size each bar. First set position size to 0 if any risk condition is true: df['close'] < df['sma_200'] OR df['std_20'] > 0.06 OR df['atr_14'] > 0.03 * df['close'] OR df['close'] < df['ema_50'] - 1.5 * df['atr_14']. If the risk block is not triggered, size the entry by signal strength using all of these factors together: set size to 1.0 when df['stoch_k_14'] < 10 AND df['stoch_d_14'] < 15 AND df['rsi_14'] < 25 AND df['mfi_14'] < 25 AND df['close'] > df['sma_200']. Otherwise set size to 0.5 when df['stoch_k_14'] < 20 AND df['rsi_14'] < 35 AND df['close'] > df['sma_200'] AND df['ma_50'] < 1.02; else set size to 0.25 when df['stoch_k_14'] < 30 AND df['close'] > df['ema_50'] AND df['mfi_14'] < 40; else set size to 0. Add a profit-protection clamp with higher priority than the sizing tiers: if df['max_20'] < 1.01 AND df['rsi_14'] > 65, cap the position at 0.25 even if a stronger entry tier is true. Also force a flat exit (size 0) if df['rsi_14'] > 75 AND df['kup2'] > 0.60 to avoid buying into rejection candles.

L1_hard.summary: Fast momentum participation using MACD thrust, range position, and volume confirmation with rejection-based overrides.
L1_hard.query: Buy pressure is prioritized, but a rejection/risk override must win whenever it appears: set position size to 0 if df['macd_hist'] < 0 OR df['cntn_3'] > 0.66 OR (df['klen'] > 0.08 AND df['ksft2'] < -0.30) OR df['roc_3'] > 1.02. If not blocked, take 1.0 exposure when df['macd'] > df['macd_signal'] AND df['macd_hist'] > 0 AND df['rsv_10'] > 0.85 AND df['vma_5'] < 0.70 AND df['cord_10'] > 0.20. Otherwise take 0.5 exposure when df['macd_hist'] > 0 AND df['rsv_10'] > 0.75 AND df['vma_5'] < 0.85 AND df['rsi_14'] > 55; else take 0.25 exposure when df['ema_10'] > df['ema_30'] AND df['rsi_7'] > 60 AND df['cntp_5'] > 0.60; else take 0. If a near-exhaustion condition appears, it overrides the above sizing: whenever df['rank_20'] > 0.90 AND (df['rsi_7'] > 88 OR df['kup2'] > 0.70), cap the position at 0.25. As an additional safety brake, force size to 0 when df['vstd_20'] > 0.80 to avoid trading during unstable volume spikes.

L1_hard.summary: Volatility-bucket sizing with trend gating and pullback timing, plus distribution and breakdown priority exits.
L1_hard.query: Determine a volatility cap first, then apply signal sizing beneath it, with risk overrides always taking precedence on the same bar. Set the position size to 0 immediately if df['close'] < df['sma_100'] OR df['cci_20'] < -200 OR df['vsumd_10'] < -0.60 OR df['close'] < df['ema_20'] - 1.2 * df['atr_14']. If not flat, compute a maximum allowed size (cap) from current volatility: cap = 0.25 when df['std_20'] >= 0.07 OR df['atr_14'] > 0.04 * df['close']; cap = 0.50 when 0.04 <= df['std_20'] < 0.07; otherwise cap = 1.0. Within that cap, set desired size to 1.0 when df['close'] > df['sma_100'] AND df['ema_20'] > df['ema_50'] AND df['mfi_14'] < 35 AND df['rsv_14'] < 0.40 AND df['cntd_5'] > -0.20; set desired size to 0.5 when df['close'] > df['sma_100'] AND df['ema_20'] > df['ema_50'] AND df['mfi_14'] < 45 AND df['rsv_14'] < 0.50; set desired size to 0.25 when df['close'] > df['sma_100'] AND df['cntd_10'] > 0.10; else desired size is 0. The final position size each bar is the smaller of desired size and cap. Add a profit-throttle that can only reduce exposure: if df['rsv_14'] > 0.80 AND df['mfi_14'] > 75, cap the position at 0.25; if df['rsi_14'] > 65 AND df['ma_20'] < 1.00, cap at 0.50.

L2_easy.summary: Uptrend pullback entries with multi-confirmation and tight, volatility-aware risk exits.
L2_easy.query: The goal is to participate only in established uptrends and avoid drawdowns from unstable regimes. Require trend confirmation using df['close'] relative to a longer moving average (e.g., df['ema_50'] or df['sma_200']) and only allow entries when the faster average (e.g., df['ema_20']) is not below the slower average. Enter on a controlled pullback: df['rsi_14'] should be below a conservative “oversold-in-uptrend” threshold while price remains above the longer trend filter, and add a secondary confirmation such as df['mfi_14'] staying above a low “capitulation” level. Set position size conservatively: use a smaller allocation when only the pullback signal is present, and increase toward full size only when momentum confirmation agrees (e.g., df['macd'] > df['macd_signal']). Exit immediately on risk breakdown (e.g., df['close'] falling below the trend filter or closing below df['bb_lower_20']), and take profits when price reaches an upper-band stretch (df['close'] near df['bb_upper_20']) or df['rsi_14'] reaches an inferred overbought zone. Add a volatility gate using df['std_20'] so trades are avoided or downsized when volatility is elevated.

L2_easy.summary: Volume-confirmed breakouts that scale in early and ride momentum with wider exits.
L2_easy.query: Buy when momentum appears early and accept more false signals in exchange for capturing outsized runs. Use a breakout trigger such as df['close'] pushing above df['bb_upper_20'] or a strong trend alignment where df['ema_20'] > df['ema_50'], then require at least one fast momentum check (e.g., df['macd_hist'] > 0 or df['stoch_k_14'] > df['stoch_d_14']). Confirm participation with volume expansion by enforcing a “volume surge” condition using df['vma_20'] (below a chosen threshold implies current volume above its recent mean) and/or df['vsumd_10'] being meaningfully positive. Position sizing should be assertive: allocate more when both breakout and volume conditions are present, and reduce when only price momentum is present without volume confirmation. Use a wider failure exit to avoid getting shaken out: abandon the signal if df['close'] falls back below df['bb_middle_20'] or if momentum flips (e.g., df['macd_hist'] turns negative), and optionally de-risk when df['rsi_14'] is in an inferred extreme overbought region. Include a simple churn-control rule by skipping new entries when df['klen'] indicates an unusually large candle (interpreted as elevated gap/range risk).

L2_easy.summary: Regime-aware blend of mean reversion and trend following with volatility-scaled exposure.
L2_easy.query: This approach aims for consistent profitability by switching behavior based on a current-bar volatility regime. Define the regime using df['std_20']: when volatility is low (below an inferred threshold), favor mean reversion; when volatility is high (above that threshold), favor trend continuation. In the low-volatility regime, enter when df['close'] is near or below df['bb_lower_20'] with df['rsi_14'] in an oversold area, and plan exits toward df['bb_middle_20'] (or df['bb_upper_20'] for stronger rebounds). In the high-volatility regime, enter only with directional confirmation (e.g., df['ema_20'] > df['ema_50'] and df['macd'] > df['macd_signal']) to avoid fading strong moves, and exit on trend deterioration (e.g., df['ema_20'] <= df['ema_50'] or df['close'] slipping below df['ema_20']). Make position size adaptive: scale down exposure as df['std_20'] rises, and allow larger size when volatility is subdued and signals align. Add a universal risk override using df['atr_14'] as a sanity check: if current range conditions imply abnormal risk (ATR unusually large relative to recent behavior), require stricter confirmations or stay flat for that bar.

L2_easy.summary: Bollinger-band mean reversion with hammer confirmation and volatility-gated risk sizing.
L2_easy.query: Prioritize capital preservation by only acting on clear exhaustion signals at statistical extremes. Enter when df['close'] is below df['bb_lower_{n}'] and an oversold oscillator (use df['rsi_{n}'] or df['mfi_{n}']) confirms selling pressure is stretched, while the candle shows rejection (e.g., elevated df['klow2'] and non-negative df['kmid2']). Add a volatility gate: if df['std_{n}'] is above a chosen ceiling, either skip the trade or cap position size to a small fraction. Exit on mean reversion toward df['bb_middle_{n}'] and/or when the oscillator normalizes back toward its mid-range, whichever occurs first. Include a hard “risk-off” exit whenever df['close'] falls decisively further below df['bb_lower_{n}'] in combination with rising df['std_{n}'] (thresholds to be selected conservatively).

L2_easy.summary: Fast momentum ignition using MACD trigger, range expansion, and volume participation filters.
L2_easy.query: Buy quickly when momentum flips from negative to positive: use df['macd'] crossing above df['macd_signal'] as the primary trigger. Require a price-impulse candle to validate urgency (e.g., df['klen'] above a selected expansion threshold and df['kmid'] positive), and confirm participation via a volume surge proxy such as df['vma_{n}'] falling below a chosen level and/or df['cord_{n}'] turning positive. Let position size scale up with signal strength, for example allocating more when df['macd_hist'] is strongly positive and df['rsv_{n}'] is rising toward its upper region. Exit rapidly on momentum failure: df['macd'] crossing back below df['macd_signal'] or an overbought oscillator reversal (use df['stoch_k_{n}'] vs df['stoch_d_{n}']). Use a wider volatility allowance by only forcing an immediate flat signal under extreme adverse movement conditions defined by a high df['std_{n}'] combined with bearish candle structure (e.g., negative df['kmid2']).

L2_easy.summary: Oscillator swing entries with confirmation from return persistence and volatility-adjusted exposure.
L2_easy.query: This approach aims for steady swing captures by combining an oscillator turn with evidence that short-term returns are stabilizing. Enter when df['stoch_k_{n}'] crosses above df['stoch_d_{n}'] from a low zone (oversold threshold to be chosen) and short-horizon return balance improves (e.g., df['sumd_{n}'] turning positive or df['cntd_{n}'] rising above a small positive cutoff). Add a sanity filter so trades are avoided when df['wvma_{n}'] or df['std_{n}'] indicates unusually noisy conditions; alternatively, reduce exposure proportionally as these volatility measures increase. Take profits when the stochastic reaches an upper zone (overbought threshold to be chosen) or when price becomes statistically stretched (e.g., df['qtlu_{n}'] exceeds a selected level). Exit defensively when df['stoch_k_{n}'] crosses back below df['stoch_d_{n}'] or when return balance deteriorates (df['sumd_{n}']/df['cntd_{n}'] falls below its neutral line).

L2_easy.summary: Trade only established trends, filtered by low volatility and non-overbought momentum confirmation.
L2_easy.query: The objective is steady trend capture with strict risk control and low trade frequency. Generate an entry signal only when a short EMA is above a long EMA (use df['ema_{n1}'] > df['ema_{n2}'] with n1 < n2) AND volatility is calm (df['std_{n3}'] below a conservative cutoff) AND momentum is supportive but not stretched (df['rsi_{n4}'] in a neutral-to-bullish zone rather than overbought). Add a participation filter so signals are ignored on abnormal volume spikes (e.g., require df['vma_{n5}'] not to indicate extreme one-bar volume). Exit when trend quality deteriorates (close falls below a medium trend anchor such as df['sma_{n6}']) or when a volatility-based stop is hit (use df['atr_{n7}'] as the risk yardstick with a relatively tight multiple). Optionally take partial profits when price becomes extended versus df['bb_upper_{n8}'] while keeping the remainder only if the EMA trend condition still holds.

L2_easy.summary: Attack explosive momentum days using wide-range bullish candles near highs with volume confirmation.
L2_easy.query: Buy when price shows a breakout-like impulse on the current bar: the close is near the rolling window high (df['max_{n1}'] close to 1.0 and df['rank_{n1}'] high) AND the candle is a strong bullish range expansion (df['klen'] elevated with df['kmid2'] strongly positive). Require momentum confirmation via df['cci_{n2}'] being decisively positive (choose a high threshold consistent with “strong trend”). To avoid illiquid pops, also require a volume surge condition (df['vma_{n3}'] sufficiently below 1.0) so the move is volume-backed. Exit quickly on momentum failure signals such as a sharp bearish reversal candle (df['kmid2'] meaningfully negative) or df['cci_{n2}'] dropping back toward/under zero, but allow room for noise by using a wider ATR-based stop multiple with df['atr_{n4}']. Include an optional profit-taking rule that triggers when price becomes extremely stretched (e.g., rsi via df['rsi_{n5}'] enters an overbought zone) while keeping re-entry allowed whenever the impulse conditions reappear.

L2_easy.summary: Use volume-price participation as a gate, then ride trends with volatility-scaled position sizing.
L2_easy.query: This approach trades only when participation is healthy, then balances trend-following with adaptive risk. First, require a positive and sufficiently strong price/volume co-movement regime using df['cord_{n1}'] (delta-close vs delta-volume correlation above a chosen cutoff); otherwise, generate no entry signal. Within that regime, generate an entry signal when trend and location agree: close above df['sma_{n2}'] and also supported by mean-vs-price positioning (df['ma_{n2}'] below 1.0), while df['rsv_{n3}'] indicates price is in the upper portion of its recent range but not at the extreme. Set position size dynamically using current volatility: scale exposure down as df['std_{n4}'] increases (define two or three bands for full/half/minimal size). Exit when participation fades (df['cord_{n1}'] falls below the gate) or when price loses its trend anchor (close below df['bb_middle_{n5}'] or below df['sma_{n2}']), with an additional ATR-based protective stop using df['atr_{n6}'] to prevent large losses during sudden volatility spikes.

L2_easy.summary: Trend-filtered dip entries using RSI/MFI confirmation and correlation-based risk control.
L2_easy.query: Prioritize capital preservation by only taking signals aligned with a primary uptrend filter such as df['close'] > df['sma_200']. Enter on a controlled pullback where df['close'] is not extended above a medium-term anchor (e.g., near df['ema_20'] or df['sma_50']) while df['rsi_14'] is in a “reset but not broken” zone (above a classic oversold level yet below neutral) and df['mfi_14'] indicates fresh buying interest (choose a conservative threshold range). Require a supportive price/volume relationship by gating entries with df['cord_20'] > 0 (or a similarly chosen lookback) and avoid turbulent periods by filtering out bars where df['std_20'] exceeds a low-volatility cutoff you set. Exit defensively when df['close'] falls below df['sma_50'] or when df['cord_20'] turns negative, and take profits when df['qtlu_60'] becomes meaningfully positive (price pressing above its upper quantile) or df['rsi_14'] reaches a conservative overbought zone. Keep the stop tight by defining a volatility-aware fail-safe using df['atr_14'] (choose a small multiple consistent with the conservative mandate).

L2_easy.summary: Capitulation-reversal entries using CCI extremes, strong close location, and volume shock confirmation.
L2_easy.query: Buy reversal strength quickly after apparent capitulation: look for df['cci_20'] at an extreme negative level (select the cutoff) combined with a strong close location such as df['ksft2'] well above zero (close skewed toward the high of the bar). Demand participation by requiring unusually high activity via df['vma_20'] < 1 (current volume above its average) or elevated df['vstd_20'] (choose which volume shock proxy you prefer and set the threshold). To reduce “one-bar wonders,” add a momentum alignment check like df['stoch_k_14'] > df['stoch_d_14'] while df['rsv_14'] is above a midline level you specify. Use signal strength to size up: the more extreme df['cci_20'] and the stronger the volume shock, the larger the allocation; otherwise keep it smaller. Exit on a wide, volatility-based risk limit using df['atr_14'] (larger multiple than conservative), and take profits when df['cci_20'] swings to a high positive extreme or when df['rsv_14'] approaches the top of its range (e.g., near the upper decile).

L2_easy.summary: Volatility-aware dual-mode strategy: trend continuation in calm markets, stabilization entries in noisy markets.
L2_easy.query: Start with a regime split driven only by current-bar volatility: treat df['std_20'] below a chosen cutoff as “calm” and df['std_20'] above it as “noisy.” In calm conditions, participate in trend continuation by entering when df['rank_60'] is elevated (price holding near the top of its medium-term distribution) and df['corr_30'] is positive, suggesting price and volume levels are moving in sync. In noisy conditions, shift to stabilization entries by requiring df['rsv_20'] to be depressed (near the lower part of the recent high-low range) while df['rsi_14'] stays above a deep-oversold floor, aiming to avoid pure free-fall bars. Scale exposure adaptively using activity-driven uncertainty: allocate more when df['wvma_20'] is low (cleaner movement) and reduce size when df['wvma_20'] is high (choppy, volume-weighted volatility). Exit with a clear priority rule: if df['wvma_20'] spikes above a risk threshold or df['corr_30'] flips negative, flatten regardless of entry style; otherwise take profits when df['rank_60'] falls back toward the middle region or df['rsi_14'] reaches a moderate overbought band you define.

L2_easy.summary: Buy near 52-week highs in calm volatility, exit on volatility spikes or trend loss.
L2_easy.query: The objective is to participate only in high-quality uptrends while minimizing drawdowns. Enter when price is behaving like a “52-week high leader”: df['max_252'] is close to 1.0 (price near its 252-day high) and trend bias is positive via df['ma_100'] < 1.0 (price above its 100-day average). Add a risk filter that requires a volatility contraction using df['std_20'] below a conservative cutoff, and avoid chasing by requiring df['rsi_14'] to be strong but not “overbought” (pick a reasonable upper band). Exit on any sign of deterioration: price no longer near highs (df['max_252'] meaningfully above 1.0) or a volatility expansion (df['std_20'] jumps above its risk cutoff) or momentum loss (df['rsi_14'] falls below a neutral threshold). Use an ATR-based protective stop referenced to df['atr_14'] with a relatively tight multiple consistent with capital preservation, and size positions smaller when df['std_20'] is higher even if entry conditions are met.

L2_easy.summary: Exploit momentum bursts with volume surge and strong closes, riding until momentum fades.
L2_easy.query: Buy when a momentum burst is underway and the day closes with clear dominance. Define the burst using a short-horizon rate-of-change (df['roc_3'] or df['roc_5'] indicating strong upside), require trend agreement with a fast EMA above a slower EMA (e.g., df['ema_10'] > df['ema_30']), and confirm urgency with a volume surge via df['vma_20'] being meaningfully below 1.0 (current volume above average). To ensure you are not buying weak rallies, require a strong close location such as df['ksft2'] being high (close near the high of the bar), and allow entries even when oscillators are elevated (do not over-filter). Exit quickly when the thrust fails: df['macd_hist'] turns negative or df['rsv_14'] drops back below a mid-range “loss of control” level. Risk controls should be wider than conservative styles, using a larger ATR multiple on df['atr_14'], and optionally scale exposure up when both df['roc_5'] and df['vma_20'] confirm exceptional momentum.

L2_easy.summary: Follow trends only when price and volume changes agree, with volatility-scaled exposure and exits.
L2_easy.query: When price and volume are aligned, the strategy seeks steady trend capture with adaptive risk. Enter on trend confirmation using a medium-term moving-average structure (e.g., df['ema_20'] > df['ema_60'] and df['close'] above df['ema_20']) and require participation confirmation using df['cord_20'] positive (price-change and volume-change moving together) or df['vsumd_20'] positive (volume pressure skewed upward). Add a simple “avoid churn” filter that blocks new entries when df['std_20'] is too high for the instrument, but do not require extremely low volatility—this is meant to trade regularly, not only in squeezes. Position sizing must be volatility-aware on the current bar: take a larger allocation when df['std_20'] is low and a reduced allocation when df['std_20'] is elevated, while still honoring the same entry logic. Exit on trend failure (df['close'] falling below df['ema_60']) or on participation breakdown (df['cord_20'] turning negative), with an ATR-based stop using df['atr_14'] and a moderate profit-taking rule triggered by an oscillator reaching a “crowded” zone (choose an RSI or MFI level consistent with taking profits without cutting winners too early).

L2_easy.summary: Quantile-based bargain entries within an uptrend, with tight ATR risk controls and time stop.
L2_easy.query: Prioritize risk first: only allow exposure when volatility is contained (df['atr_{n}'] and/or df['std_{n}'] below a conservative threshold). Enter on a “discount” setup where df['qtld_{n}'] is sufficiently negative (price below its lower quantile zone) while the primary trend filter is positive (df['sma_{n_long}'] rising or df['close'] > df['sma_{n_long}']). Add a simple accumulation confirmation by requiring df['mfi_{n}'] to be above its neutral midline and improving relative to a modest threshold. Exit immediately on a tight ATR-based stop (a small multiple of df['atr_{n}'] below df['close']) or if trend support fails (df['close'] < df['sma_{n_long}']). Take profits when df['qtlu_{n}'] turns positive beyond a modest threshold (price into the upper quantile zone) or when df['rsi_{n}'] reaches an overbought region. Include a time-based exit: if the rebound does not materialize within a short holding window, flatten to preserve capital.

L2_easy.summary: Squeeze-to-expansion breakout that sizes up with momentum strength and exits on momentum fade.
L2_easy.query: Buy on a volatility-squeeze breakout: require df['std_{n}'] to be unusually low (compression) and df['close'] to close above df['bb_upper_{n}'] (expansion trigger). To act early, accept the first clean breakout bar even without additional confirmation, but scale position size by momentum strength using df['macd_hist'] (larger when clearly positive, smaller when near zero). Add a price-location filter so breakouts are “real”: df['rsv_{n}'] should be high (close near the top of the recent range) and df['klen'] should indicate a wide real range relative to open. Exit on momentum fade (df['macd_hist'] flipping negative or df['close'] falling back under df['bb_middle_{n}']) and use a wider trailing stop tied to df['atr_{n}'] to stay in fast trends. If df['rsi_{n}'] becomes extremely overbought, allow partial profit-taking while keeping a residual position as long as the breakout condition remains valid.

L2_easy.summary: Uptrend dip-buys timed by recent-window extrema, with volatility-scaled sizing and regime-aware exits.
L2_easy.query: Design a medium-frequency approach that buys pullbacks inside an uptrend, but only when the pullback is “fresh”: require df['ema_{n_fast}'] > df['ema_{n_slow}'] and df['imin_{n}'] to be small (the window’s low occurred very recently). Confirm the dip is stabilizing rather than collapsing by demanding df['rank_{n}'] is no longer at the very bottom of its range and df['cntd_{n}'] is not strongly negative. Set position size adaptively: use larger size when df['atr_{n}'] (or df['std_{n}']) is low-to-moderate, and reduce size materially when volatility is elevated. Exit in two regimes determined on the current bar: in calm volatility, take profit when df['imax_{n}'] is small (recent high printed) and df['rsi_{n}'] is stretched; in high volatility, prioritize protection by exiting on df['close'] < df['ema_{n_fast}'] or a tighter ATR stop. Add a modest time stop to prevent capital being tied up in slow drifts that never revert.

L2_easy.summary: Trade volatility-contraction breakouts in uptrends with strict, fast risk-off exits.
L2_easy.query: The objective is steady compounding by only participating in calm, established uptrends and avoiding noisy conditions. Enter when price is above a long-term trend anchor (df['sma_{n}'] or df['ema_{n}']) and volatility is clearly contracted using df['std_{n}'] (optionally confirmed by muted volume dispersion via df['vstd_{n}']). Require a “quiet strength” confirmation: close should be positioned in the upper part of its recent range (df['rsv_{n}'] high) without being aggressively overbought (df['rsi_{n}'] in a controlled bullish zone). Use smaller default sizing, and reduce exposure further whenever df['std_{n}'] rises above its calm-regime cutoff. Exit quickly if the trend filter fails (close back below the chosen df['sma_{n}']/df['ema_{n}']) or if volatility re-expands (df['std_{n}'] jumps) while momentum weakens (df['rsv_{n}'] drops toward mid-range).

L2_easy.summary: Exploit momentum acceleration using beta, rank, and volume participation for fast trend rides.
L2_easy.query: Buy when short-horizon price acceleration is strong (df['beta_{n}'] indicates a sharp upward drift) and the stock is already pressing the top of its recent distribution (df['rank_{n}'] high). Add a participation gate so moves are not “empty”: require improving return asymmetry (df['sumd_{n}'] positive) and supportive volume asymmetry (df['vsumd_{n}'] positive), allowing parameters and cutoffs to be selected for higher signal frequency. Position size should scale up when momentum confirmation is strongest (e.g., df['macd_hist'] firmly positive) and scale down when momentum is only marginal. Exit on momentum deterioration rather than waiting for a full trend break: df['macd_hist'] turning negative, df['beta_{n}'] reverting toward zero/positive, or df['rank_{n}'] falling out of its high zone. Include a wide, volatility-aware “give it room” constraint by reducing (not necessarily closing) exposure when df['std_{n}'] spikes, to avoid getting chopped during abrupt reversals.

L2_easy.summary: Blend trend-following and tactical pullbacks with regime-aware sizing driven by volatility and flow.
L2_easy.query: This approach alternates between trend continuation and tactical pullback entries using a simple current-bar regime test. When momentum regime is positive (df['macd_hist'] > 0), prefer continuation entries aligned with the trend (close above a medium-term df['ema_{n}']) and avoid chasing: look for mild pullback/mean reversion signals such as df['ma_{n}'] rising above 1.0 while df['rsi_{n}'] remains constructive. When momentum regime is negative or neutral (df['macd_hist'] near/below 0), only take smaller “reversion-to-fair” entries if selling pressure looks exhausted (df['stoch_k_{n}'] recovering from a low zone and/or df['cntd_{n}'] improving toward positive). Size dynamically: increase exposure in low-volatility conditions (df['std_{n}'] low) and cut exposure as volatility rises; optionally add a second risk scaler using df['wvma_{n}'] to downshift during unstable volume-weighted moves. Exits should be symmetric to the regime: in trend mode, exit on loss of trend alignment (close below df['ema_{n}'] or df['macd_hist'] flips negative); in reversion mode, exit into strength once oscillators normalize (df['stoch_k_{n}'] reaches a high zone or df['ma_{n}'] returns toward 1.0).

L2_easy.summary: Trend-aligned stochastic reversal entries with strict ATR risk control and partial profit-taking.
L2_easy.query: Prioritize capital preservation by only taking pullback reversals inside an established uptrend: require df['close'] > df['sma_200']. Enter when df['stoch_k_14'] crosses above df['stoch_d_14'] from an oversold zone (choose the oversold threshold) and confirm participation by requiring df['cord_20'] > 0. Keep trading frequency low by adding a calm-market filter such as df['std_20'] below a chosen cutoff. Take partial profits when df['close'] reaches df['bb_middle_20'], and fully exit on trend weakness (e.g., df['close'] < df['ema_20'] or a bearish stochastic cross from an overbought zone). Use a tight protective stop based on a small multiple of df['atr_14'], and do not allow any entry signal to override the stop condition.

L2_easy.summary: Fast momentum swing entries using short EMA thrust, CCI impulse, and volume surprise confirmation.
L2_easy.query: Buy quickly when a short-term momentum thrust appears: require a fast/slow EMA alignment (e.g., df['ema_5'] > df['ema_13']) and a momentum impulse via df['cci_20'] breaking above a chosen trigger level. Add a volume-surprise gate by demanding df['vma_20'] be sufficiently low (current volume well above its recent average; choose the cutoff) to justify acting early. To avoid choppy setups, optionally require df['rank_20'] to be in the upper portion of its range (select the threshold) so entries occur near short-window strength. Exit fast on loss of thrust—such as df['macd_hist'] turning negative or df['close'] falling back under the slow EMA—without waiting for additional confirmation. Use a wider stop than conservative approaches, set as a larger multiple of df['atr_14'], and allow frequent re-entries whenever the same conditions reappear.

L2_easy.summary: Liquidity-regime strategy: trend-follow in stable volume, mean-revert in unstable volume, volatility-scaled exposure.
L2_easy.query: This approach adapts behavior based on a liquidity/participation regime defined by df['vstd_20']: treat low df['vstd_20'] as stable participation and high df['vstd_20'] as unstable participation (choose the split). In the stable regime, enter on trend continuation when df['ema_20'] > df['sma_50'] and df['mfi_14'] is above a selected midline threshold, aiming to ride directional flow. In the unstable regime, shift to controlled mean-reversion: buy when df['close'] is near/below df['bb_lower_20'] and df['rsi_14'] is recovering upward from an oversold area (select the oversold and recovery triggers). Scale position size inversely with df['std_20'] (bigger in lower price volatility, smaller in higher volatility) while keeping a hard stop at a chosen multiple of df['atr_14']. Exit rules should match the active regime: trend-mode exits on df['ema_20'] falling below df['sma_50'] or df['mfi_14'] dropping under the midline, and mean-reversion exits at df['bb_middle_20'] or when df['rsi_14'] reaches an overbought threshold.

L2_easy.summary: Trend-filtered wick-reversal entries with tight ATR risk and conservative sizing.
L2_easy.query: The strategy targets low-frequency, high-quality reversal entries while preserving capital. Enter when price is above a long-term trend filter (e.g., df['sma_{L}'] or df['ema_{L}']) AND a bullish rejection candle appears (use df['klow2'] elevated with df['kmid'] > 0) AND a momentum oscillator signals oversold (e.g., df['rsi_{n}'] below an oversold band such as 25–35). Require a volatility sanity check so entries only occur when df['std_{v}'] is not elevated relative to its typical range (choose a simple threshold). Position sizing should be small by default and increased only when both oversold + wick-rejection are strong (e.g., deeper RSI + larger lower wick implies larger size). Exit immediately on a volatility spike (df['atr_{a}'] or df['std_{v}'] jumping above a chosen risk threshold) or when price loses the trend filter (close below the long-term MA). Add a tight ATR-based stop distance (multiple to be inferred) and allow partial profit-taking when the oscillator mean-reverts toward neutral.

L2_easy.summary: Fast breakout ignition using volume surge, bullish range expansion, and MACD confirmation.
L2_easy.query: Buy early into momentum ignitions: trigger an entry when the close is pressing recent highs (df['max_{n}'] close to 1.0 and/or df['rank_{n}'] in the top portion of its range) while the candle shows range expansion and directional strength (high df['klen'] with df['kmid'] strongly positive). Confirm with participation by requiring unusually high current volume versus its average (df['vma_{n}'] well below 1.0) and a momentum shift via MACD (df['macd_hist'] positive and improving). Use larger position sizes when both breakout strength (rank/max) and volume surprise (vma) align; otherwise use a smaller “probe” size. Exit quickly if momentum stalls (df['macd_hist'] fades toward zero), or if price falls back under a fast moving average (df['ema_{f}']) used as a trailing reference. Set a wider protective stop using an ATR multiple (df['atr_{a}']) to tolerate noise, but force a hard risk-off if volatility explodes (df['atr_{a}'] relative to price becomes extreme).

L2_easy.summary: Volatility-aware trend participation using Bollinger support, stochastic timing, and adaptive sizing.
L2_easy.query: This approach aims for steady compounding by participating in trends while scaling risk to current volatility. Define a regime each bar using a volatility gauge (df['std_{v}'] or df['atr_{a}'] relative to price) and size positions inversely to that regime (larger in calmer conditions, smaller when volatile). Enter when price is trading above the Bollinger middle band (df['bb_middle_{n}']) but pulls back toward it without breaking down, and the stochastic oscillator turns up from a mid-to-low zone (df['stoch_k_{n}'] recovering and above df['stoch_d_{n}'], with thresholds to be inferred). Add a flow filter so entries prefer supportive money flow (df['mfi_{n}'] not overbought and improving) to reduce chasing. Take partial profits when price stretches toward the upper band (df['bb_upper_{n}']) or when stochastic reaches an upper zone, while keeping a residual position for continuation. Exit the remainder when price closes back below the Bollinger middle band or when volatility jumps into the high-risk regime, whichever occurs first.

L2_easy.summary: Trend-filtered pullback entries using RSI and MFI with volatility-gated, defensive sizing and exits.
L2_easy.query: The strategy seeks conservative participation in an established uptrend by buying controlled pullbacks. Define the primary trend using a long lookback moving average (e.g., df['sma_{L}']) and only consider entries when df['close'] is above that trend filter and realized volatility is subdued via df['std_{V}'] (choose L and V). Trigger an entry when both df['rsi_{n}'] and df['mfi_{n}'] indicate oversold conditions (select the lookback n and oversold thresholds), with position size scaled by signal depth (e.g., smaller size for mild oversold, larger size for deeper oversold) and further reduced when df['std_{V}'] is elevated. Exit defensively when the pullback thesis is invalidated (df['close'] falls below df['sma_{L}']) or when momentum normalizes (df['rsi_{n}'] mean-reverts to a neutral zone), and include a “stagnation” exit when df['beta_{b}'] fails to stay positive over a chosen horizon b. Add a tight volatility-aware risk cut using df['atr_{a}'] by requiring price to stay within an acceptable ATR distance of a reference average (e.g., df['ema_{f}']); if it deviates beyond a chosen multiple, exit.

L2_easy.summary: High-frequency momentum entries when price hugs the range top and breadth stays strongly positive.
L2_easy.query: Buy fast momentum bursts when the market is already pressing the top of its recent range and the tape stays one-sided. Use df['rsv_{n}'] as the primary trigger (enter when it is in the upper band of its 0–1 range) and require short-horizon participation via df['cntp_{m}'] or df['cntd_{m}'] to confirm that most recent returns are positive (pick n and m). To avoid chasing noisy spikes, gate entries with a “quality” filter that prefers lower churn, such as df['wvma_{q}'] staying below a chosen ceiling, while allowing higher trading frequency than conservative setups (choose q and the ceiling). Exits should be quick: take profits when df['rsv_{n}'] falls back toward the midrange or when df['cntd_{m}'] flips meaningfully negative, and add a momentum failure exit when df['kmid'] turns bearish on the current bar. Risk control should be wider than conservative but objective: exit when df['close'] drops below df['ema_{f}'] by more than a chosen multiple of df['atr_{a}'] (select f, a, and the multiple).

L2_easy.summary: Regime-aware entries blending trend confirmation with price–volume coupling and volatility-scaled exposure.
L2_easy.query: When volatility is calm, the strategy aims to ride directional moves; when volatility is high, it shifts to tighter selectivity and smaller sizing. Detect the regime on the current bar using df['std_{v}'] (choose v and define low- vs high-volatility bands). In the low-vol regime, enter on trend alignment using a fast/slow average structure (e.g., df['ema_{f}'] above df['ema_{s}']) plus positive price–volume coupling (df['cord_{c}'] above a chosen threshold), and avoid late entries by requiring df['rsi_{r}'] to be in a constructive but not extreme zone (choose f, s, c, r and their thresholds). In the high-vol regime, keep the same directional bias but demand stronger confirmation (e.g., df['cci_{k}'] above a positive trigger and df['vstd_{u}'] not elevated) and cut position size proportionally as df['std_{v}'] increases (choose k and u). Exit rules are unified across regimes: flatten when df['ema_{f}'] no longer exceeds df['ema_{s}'] or when df['cord_{c}'] turns negative, and add a volatility shock-off switch that forces an exit or minimum size when df['std_{v}'] jumps into the high band.

L2_easy.summary: Trend-pullback entries with price–volume confirmation and strict volatility-gated risk controls.
L2_easy.query: Focus on capital preservation by only trading in an established uptrend: require a fast/slow moving-average filter such as df['ema_{fast}'] > df['ema_{slow}'] and price holding above df['sma_{slow}'] (periods to be selected). Enter on a controlled pullback rather than chasing highs, defined by df['ma_{mid}'] modestly above 1.0 (close below its mid-term mean by a small margin) while price–volume confirmation remains supportive (df['corr_{n}'] positive and above a mild threshold). Add a volatility gate so signals are ignored when df['std_{n}'] or df['atr_{n}'] is elevated versus its typical level (choose the exact cutoff). Position size should be conservative by default and only scale up when both the pullback condition and the correlation confirmation are strong; otherwise use a reduced allocation. Exit defensively when trend integrity breaks (close below df['ema_{slow}'] or df['ema_{fast}'] <= df['ema_{slow}']) or when df['corr_{n}'] turns meaningfully negative, and apply a tight ATR-based stop calibrated to current df['atr_{n}'].

L2_easy.summary: Fast momentum bursts triggered by range expansion candles and volume surprise near highs.
L2_easy.query: Buy quickly when a momentum ignition candle appears: a large bullish body (df['kmid2'] clearly positive) combined with range expansion (df['klen'] above a chosen threshold) and price closing near the top of its recent range (df['rsv_{n}'] high, e.g., upper-quartile behavior). Require a volume surprise confirmation using df['vma_{n}'] substantially below 1.0 (current volume above its average) to avoid low-liquidity pops; the exact level is to be inferred. Add a light trend bias so the strongest signals occur when df['ema_{fast}'] is above df['ema_{slow}'], but allow trades even without full alignment if the candle and volume criteria are extreme. Use a wider ATR-based stop (multiple of df['atr_{n}']) to tolerate noise, and take profits opportunistically when short-horizon momentum becomes stretched (e.g., df['roc_{n}'] indicates an unusually fast rise or df['rsv_{n}'] stops staying elevated). Exit immediately on momentum failure signals such as df['kmid2'] flipping negative or a sharp drop in df['rsv_{n}'] back toward mid-range, even if the stop has not been hit.

L2_easy.summary: Quiet accumulation near highs using money flow and price–volume coupling with adaptive sizing.
L2_easy.query: This approach targets steady profitability by entering during quiet accumulation phases: price should be close to its rolling high (df['max_{n}'] near 1.0, with the exact proximity threshold chosen) while realized volatility is contained (df['std_{n}'] below a moderate cutoff). Confirm that buying pressure is present using df['mfi_{n}'] above a neutral level and improving price–volume coupling via df['cord_{n}'] being positive (select lookbacks/levels). To avoid buying late-stage blow-offs, filter out entries when df['rsi_{n}'] is already at an extreme overbought zone; keep the ceiling as a tunable parameter. Position sizing should adapt to current risk: scale exposure inversely with df['atr_{n}'] or df['std_{n}'] (smaller size when volatility is higher), and optionally add a small size boost when both MFI and cord are strong. Exit when accumulation disappears (df['mfi_{n}'] falls back below neutral or df['cord_{n}'] turns negative), or when price slips meaningfully away from the highs (df['max_{n}'] rises above a drawdown threshold), with an ATR-based stop as a final safety net.

L2_easy.summary: Trade only established uptrends with volume-confirmed participation and volatility-gated risk controls.
L2_easy.query: The strategy should participate only in well-established uptrends, defined by a fast/slow moving-average alignment using df['ema_{fast}'] versus df['ema_{slow}'] (choose common periods). Enter when trend is up and participation is supportive: require df['corr_{n}'] to be meaningfully positive and df['vma_{n}'] to indicate volume is not abnormally thin (select a reasonable threshold around 1). Add a stability gate so new entries are allowed only when df['std_{n}'] is below a conservative ceiling (set to avoid high-volatility whipsaws). Exit defensively if the trend filter fails (fast EMA falls back below slow EMA) or if df['corr_{n}'] turns negative, signaling weakening price–volume coupling. Include a tight ATR-based risk stop using df['atr_{n}'] (choose a small multiple) and a time-based exit that closes the trade after a fixed number of bars if momentum does not progress.

L2_easy.summary: Exploit capitulation-style selloffs for sharp snapback rallies using quantiles and downside-breadth measures.
L2_easy.query: Buy the snapback after a capitulation-like selloff identified by extreme downside stretch: df['qtld_{n}'] should be sufficiently negative (set an aggressive extreme threshold) and df['min_{n}'] should indicate price is very close to its window low. To increase hit rate in fast reversals, require downside breadth to be elevated using df['cntn_{n}'] and/or df['sumn_{n}'] (choose high cutoffs that imply most recent returns were negative). Add a “selling exhaustion” filter by demanding df['vstd_{n}'] to be elevated (panic-like) or, alternatively, df['vsumn_{n}'] to be high (heavy negative volume pressure); pick one and tune thresholds to keep trading frequency high but not constant. Take profits quickly into mean reversion by exiting when df['qtld_{n}'] reverts toward zero or when price reaches a short-term average such as df['sma_{n}'] (choose a short lookback). Use a wider protective stop than conservative systems, expressed as a larger multiple of df['atr_{n}'], and include an early-fail exit if df['cntd_{n}'] remains strongly negative (downside dominance persists).

L2_easy.summary: Switch between momentum-following and mean-reversion based on a current-bar volatility regime filter.
L2_easy.query: This approach should first classify the current bar into a volatility regime using df['std_{n}'] and/or df['atr_{n}'] (define a clear threshold that separates “quiet” from “active” conditions). In the active regime, trade momentum by requiring a positive MACD state (df['macd'] above df['macd_signal'] and/or df['macd_hist'] above zero) plus a supportive price location filter such as df['rank_{n}'] being relatively high (select a realistic cutoff below 1.0). In the quiet regime, trade controlled mean reversion by entering on mild oversold signals using df['rsi_{n}'] (choose a mid-level oversold threshold, not extreme) while avoiding overcrowded downside by requiring df['cntd_{n}'] to be near-neutral or improving. Exits should mirror the regime logic: momentum trades exit on MACD deterioration (histogram flip or macd crossing below signal), while mean-reversion trades exit when RSI normalizes or price returns toward a moving average (e.g., df['ema_{n}'] or df['sma_{n}']). Position size must adapt to volatility on the current bar, scaling down as df['std_{n}'] or df['atr_{n}'] increases, with a hard cap to prevent overexposure. Add a universal ATR-based stop and a profit-protecting rule that tightens exits when df['std_{n}'] spikes above the active-regime threshold.

L2_easy.summary: Trade low-volatility breakouts only when trend, range, and volume confirmation align.
L2_easy.query: The strategy targets infrequent, high-confidence upside breakouts after volatility contraction. Define an uptrend using a slow/fast moving-average filter (e.g., df['ema_{short}'] > df['ema_{long}'] or df['close'] above df['sma_{long}']), and require compression via a low normalized volatility reading (df['std_{n}'] below a conservative threshold). Enter when price breaks to a fresh window high (df['max_{m}'] very close to 1.0) and participation confirms with above-average volume (df['vma_{k}'] < 1.0, optionally also df['vstd_{k}'] not extreme). Use a tight risk stop tied to current volatility (df['atr_{n}'] multiple chosen conservatively), and exit on momentum failure such as df['close'] falling back under df['ema_{short}'] or df['max_{m}'] moving away from 1.0 (breakout rejection). Add a time-based safety exit: if the breakout does not follow through within a small fixed number of bars, flatten to reduce capital tie-up.

L2_easy.summary: Buy trend-continuation pullbacks quickly using EMA structure, bull-range RSI, and volume thrust.
L2_easy.query: Enter rapidly on continuation setups to capture large moves, accepting more false signals. Require a bullish trend structure using a fast/slow EMA stack (e.g., df['ema_{fast}'] > df['ema_{slow}']) and a “bull range” momentum filter where RSI stays above a midline floor (df['rsi_{n}'] > mid-threshold to be inferred).
